payload.rationale: The supplied official-site evidence still advertises a December 18, 2026 North American release, with international release beginning December 16 and early-access screenings December 14–15. With roughly three months remaining, that specific schedule supports a low probability of a qualifying delay past December 18. My judgment assumes that a studio-backed film maintaining detailed theatrical and IMAX dates this close to release is substantially more likely to keep its schedule than move it; this is a transfer assumption, not a measured delay rate. The strongest reason 8% could be too high is that the detailed screening schedule may reflect firm distribution commitments and considerable release readiness. The strongest reason it could be too low is that an advertised date does not establish production or post-production readiness: undisclosed technical problems or a strategic scheduling change could still force postponement. I interpret YES as a qualifying delay beyond December 18 established before the event deadline, not merely a change to an early screening.
limitations: No independent evidence establishes filming completion, post-production progress, or delivery readiness.
The evidence is one official-site snapshot; some placeholder text reduces confidence that every page element reflects finalized plans.
No historical delay base rate or fitted probability model is available.
The full frozen rules are not supplied, leaving uncertainty about the controlling release geography, announcement requirements, and treatment of a delay discovered after the cutoff.
